BILL NUMBER:  S249

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend chapter 56 of the laws of 2008 amending the general
municipal law relating to reports on the financial condition of
municipalities and to provide aid and incentives to the cities of
Rochester, Buffalo, Lackawanna, Long Beach, Syracuse, White Plains,
Yonkers and Rensselaer, in relation to aid and incentives for
municipalities (Part A); to amend the state finance law, in relation
to permitting certain public authorities to issue PIT Revenue Bonds
for any authorized purpose, within existing public authorities control
board approval requirements; to amend chapter 57 of the laws of 2008,
relating to providing for the administration of certain funds and
accounts related to the 2008-2009 budget, in relation to authorizing
the state comptroller to transfer certain monies to the general fund,
authorizing the state comptroller to deposit certain reimbursements to
the credit of any capital projects fund, and directing the dormitory
authority of the state of New York to transfer certain monies to the
general fund; to repeal subdivision (a) of section 1 of Part P of
chapter 57 of the laws of 2007 relating to providing funding for
certain community projects; and providing for the repeal of certain
provisions upon expiration thereof (Part B); to amend part NN of
chapter 57 of the laws of 2008 relating to authorizing the New York
state mortgage agency to transfer certain moneys and to amend the
private housing finance law in relation to transferring undisbursed
mortgage insurance fund reserves to the general fund and increasing
the bond issuance cap for the division of housing and community
renewal (Part C); to amend the insurance law, in relation to shifting
the costs related to the implementation of chapter 748 of the laws of
2006; and to amend chapter 748 of the laws of 2006 amending the
insurance law relating to enacting "Timothy's law", in relation to the
effectiveness of such chapter (Part D); to amend the mental hygiene
law, in relation to unified services and to repeal certain provisions
of such law relating thereto (Part E); to amend chapter 57 of the laws
of 2006, relating to establishing a cost of living adjustment for
designated human services programs, in relation to adjustments to
certain rates and the time periods for the effectiveness thereof (Part
F); to amend the public health law, in relation to the preferred drug
program; to amend the social services law and the elder law, in
relation to reimbursement to participating provider pharmacies; to
amend the public health law, in relation to reinstituting certain
hospital assessments; to amend the public health law, in relation to
reducing non-public hospital worker recruitment and retention grants;
to amend chapter 58 of the laws of 2008, amending the social services
law and the public health law relating to adjustments of rates, in
relation to hospital reimbursements and in relation to rates of
payment to nursing homes, personal care providers, certified home
health agencies (CHHAs), and long term home health care programs
(LTHHCPs); to amend the public health law, in relation to delaying
nursing home rebasing; to amend the public health law, in relation to
achieving savings in relation to nursing home, home care and personal
care rates; to amend the public health law, in relation to CHHA and
LTHHCP administrative efficiencies; to amend the public health law, in
relation to the Health Care Reform Act (HCRA) covered lives
assessment; to amend the public health law and chapter 703 of the laws
of 1988, relating to enacting the expanded health care coverage act of
nineteen hundred eighty-eight and amending the insurance law and other
laws relating to expanded health care and catastrophic health care
coverage, in relation to HCRA funding for public hospital and public
nursing home recruitment and retention grants, non-public hospital
grants, and the regional pilot program individual subsidy; to amend
the public health law, in relation to breast cancer, cancer services,
poison control and infertility; to amend the public health law, in
relation to reducing funding for the graduate medical education
professional education pool; to amend the public health law, in
relation to worker retraining funding; to amend the public health law,
in relation to increasing HCRA surcharges on hospitals and clinics; to
amend the social services law, in relation to emergency medical
transportation service supplemental payments; to amend the public
health law, in relation to reducing inpatient medical assistance rates
of payment for non-public residential healthcare facilities; to amend
the social services law, in relation to transitional supplemental
payments; to amend the public health law, in relation to medical
assistance rates of payment; to amend the social services law, in
relation to exempting persons receiving certain care from the
treatment of income and resources provisions; to amend chapter 58 of
the laws of 2007 amending the social services law and the public
health law relating to adjustments of rates, in relation to the
effectiveness thereof (Part G); relating to the transfer of funds from
the banking department account; to amend the banking law, in relation
to expenses of the banking department (Part H); relating to the
transfer of funds from the insurance department account (Part I); to
amend the executive law, in relation to authorizing the transfer of
money (Part J); and to amend the workers' compensation law, in
relation to disability payments (Part K)


 PURPOSE :
This bill enacts provisions of law that are necessary to implement
savings adjustments to the State Financial Plan. These measures have
been proposed by the Governor to address the State's projected
budgetary gaps for 2009-10 and beyond, and to help ensure 2008-09
Financial Plan balance.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Part A - Modify the Aid and Incentives for Municipalities (AIM)
Program.

This bill amends Part 0 of Chapter 56 of the Laws of 2008, which
amends the Aid and Incentives for Municipalities (AIM) Program, to
increase the amount of AIM funding that the cities of Buffalo,
Rochester, Syracuse and Yonkers may opt to receive in June, 2009
rather than in March, 2010, thereby holding those cities harmless in
their 2008-09 fiscal year for the proposed reduction in Special Aid
added to the SFY 2008-09 Enacted Budget by the Legislature.

Part B - Authorize transfers and miscellaneous capital/debt
provisions.

* This bill increases the transfer from the Environmental Protection
Fund (EPF) Transfer Account to the General Fund from $125 million to
$200 million.

* This bill increases the authority to transfer Federal child support
revenue to the General Fund, from $36 million to $136 million, in
order to achieve one-time Financial Plan relief of $100 million in SFY
2008-09.

* This bill increases the contribution to the General Fund from the
New York' Power Authority in 2008-09 from $60 million to $361 million;
establishes a $210 million payment in 2009-10; and eliminates a $35
million payment in 2010-11.

* This bill allows any public authority that is authorized to issue
Personal Income Tax (PIT) Revenue Bonds to issue debt for any other
public authorities' authorized purposes for this program, subject to
existing Public Authorities Control Board (PACB) approval
requirements. This provision is needed now, more than ever, in
response to recent crises in the financial markets that have limited
access to the capital markets, and to prevent potential negative
impacts to the Financial Plan related to reimbursing bond-financed
capital projects spending. In addition this bill amends the related
capital reimbursement provisions to permit issuer flexibility without
disrupting the existing capital responsibility of authorities.

* This bill authorizes $6.5 million in transfer authority to
accommodate a one-time transfer in reserve balance from the Dormitory
Authority Corporate Fiduciary Fund to the General Fund.

* Eliminate remaining $45 million member item funding in 2008-09.

Part C - Transfer the undisbursed balances of certain housing programs
to the General Fund.

This bill transfers, to the General Fund, the January 1, 2009
undisbursed Mortgage Insurance Fund Reserve balances for the $54
million Mitchell Lama Rehabilitation and Preservation Program and the
All Affordable Program, the $15 million Greater Catskills Flood
Remediation Program, and the $6 million Housing and Economic
Stabilization for Long Island Program (HELP) by March 31, 2009. These
programs will be bond financed as this bill also increases the
Division of Housing and Community Renewal's bond cap authorization by
$31 million, from $2.291 billion to $2.322 billion. These actions
would provide an estimated $25 million in SFY 2008-09 General Fund
relief without negatively impacting program operations.

Part D - Shift costs associated with Timothy's Law from the General
Fund to a Special Revenue Account.

This bill shifts the costs associated with the implementation of
Timothy's law, established by Chapter 748 of the laws of 2006, from
the General Fund to the Insurance Department's Special Revenue
Regulation Account. This bill also extends the effective date of
Timothy's law to December 31, 2010.

Part E - Eliminate the Differential for Unified Services in several
counties.

This bill eliminates the differential for Unified Services in five
counties (Rensselaer, Rockland, Warren, Washington, and Westchester).
In the 1970s, the Unified Services initiative began providing
additional funding to certain counties to develop a community care
system and reduce the use of State inpatient services. Currently,
there is a wide range of community-based services throughout the
State, and there is no longer justification for this differential.
Specifically, this bill achieves savings in 2008-09 totaling $700,000
growing to $2.8 million on a recurring basis.

Part F - Reduce Human Service Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA).

This bill provides for a 1 percent reduction in the 2008-09 human
services cost of living adjustment (COLA) effective January 1, 2009.
This results in a net 2.2 percent ongoing increase for 2008-09.

Part G - Health Care Savings.

This bill generates State Financial Plan relief by generating
additional revenues and reducing spending. Specifically, this bill:

* Amends Public Health law (PHL) § 272(12) to modify the Preferred
Drug Program to eliminate the exemption for anti-depressants
(anti-psychotic, anti-retroviral and anti-rejection drugs will remain
exempt);

* Amends Social Services Law (SSL) § 367-a(9)(b)(ii) to reduce
pharmacy reimbursement levels for brand name prescription drugs from

Average Wholesale Price (AWP) minus 16.25 percent to AWP minus 17.25
percent;

* Amends Elder Law § 250(1)(b)(1) to reduce pharmacy reimbursement
levels for brand name prescription drugs that are provided through the
Elderly Pharmaceutical Insurance Coverage (EPIC) program - from AWP
minus 16.25 percent to AWP minus 17.25 percent;

* Adds new PHL § 2807-d(2)(a)(vi) to reinstitute the 0.70 percent
hospital assessment;

* Adds new PHL § 2807-c(34) to reflect an across the board reduction
in hospital rates;

* Amends Chapter 58 of the Laws of 2008, Part C, § 11, and adds a new
provision to achieve savings related to general hospitals, nursing
homes, home care and personal care providers by discontinuing
remaining trend factors for calendar year 2008 and eliminating the
trend factor for calendar year 2009;

* Amends PHL § 2808(2-b) to delay nursing home rebasing until April
2009;

* Adds new PHL §§ 2808(25) and 3614(12) to achieve savings related to
across the board reductions in nursing home, home care and personal
care reimbursement rates;

* Amends PHL §§ 3614(7) and (7-a) and adds PHL § 3614(2-a) to achieve
savings by implementing administrative efficiencies for certified home
health agencies (CHHAs) and Long Term Home Health Care Programs
(LTHHCPs);

* Amends PHL § 2807-8(6)(a) to increase the amount collected through
the Health Care Reform Act (HCRA) Covered Lives Assessment;

* Amends PHL§§ 2807-c, 2808, 2807-v and 2807-1 and Chapter 703 of the
Laws of 1988 to eliminate HCRA funding for public hospital and public
nursing home recruitment and retention grants, non-public hospital
grants, and the regional pilot program individual subsidy;

* Amends PHL §§ 2807-v, 2807-1 and 2807-r to shift certain public
health care costs and certain HCRA costs to Insurance Assessments;

* Amends PHL § 2807-s to reduce Graduate Medical Education (GME)
Professional Education Pool (PEP) funding;

* Amends PHL § 2807-1 to eliminate unspent worker retraining funding;

* Amends PHL § 2807-j(2) to increase the HCRA assessments charged to
insurers;

* Amends SSL § 367-s to reduce supplemental emergency transportation
funding;

* Amends PHL § 2808 to reduce nursing home recruitment and retention
grants;

* Amends SSL §364-j-2 to reduce clinic transition payments;

* Amends PHL § 3614 to reduce rural home care payments; and

* Amends SSL § 366-c to conform with Federal requirements regarding
spousal impoverishment.

Part H - Transfer up to $6 million from the Banking Department Account
to the General Fund.
This bill authorizes the Comptroller, at the request of the Director
of the Budget, to transfer up to $6 million from the unencumbered
balance of the Banking Department Account (339.A5) to the General Fund
in State Fiscal Year 2008-09.

Part I - Transfer up to $4.5 million from the Insurance Department
Account to the General Fund.

This bill authorizes the Comptroller, at the request of the Director
of the Budget, to transfer up to $4.5 million from the unencumbered
balance of the Insurance Department Account (339.B6) to the General
Fund in State Fiscal Year 2008-09.

Part J - Transfer excess revenues from the Department of Law to the
General Fund.

This bill authorizes the transfer to the General Fund of excess
revenues, resulting from litigation settlements or prosecutions
undertaken by the Department of Law, which have accumulated in an
account dedicated for that purpose. The ongoing operations of the
Department of Law are protected by a second authorization to return
funds from the General Fund to the account - up to a total of ten
percent of the annual budget in the account - in the event revenue is
insufficient. These authorizations will allow swifter recognition of
revenues in the General Fund, while also ensuring that the ability of
the Department of Law to carry on further investigations and
litigation is not threatened.

Part K - Clarify assessments paid by insurance companies to the
Workers' Compensation Board.

This legislation would clarify the calculation of assessments
collected by the insurance industry and deposited with the Workers'
Compensation Board. At present, the basis on which assessments are
collected by the insurers currently differs from the basis on which
payments are made to the Workers' Compensation Board. As a result,
some insures collect a surplus, while others collect insufficient
funds. To the extent any insurance company has identified and held
such funds as a result of this discrepancy, such funds must be paid to
the Board and distributed according to a plan developed by the Chair
of the Workers' Compensation Board and approved by the Director of the
Budget. Funds in excess of the plan developed by the Chair may be
transferred to the General Fund.

ON' STATEMENT IN SUPPORT :
___
Enactment of these provisions is necessary to produce savings to
ensure current year budget balance, guard against further revenue
reductions and address the projected Budget gaps.

 BUDGETARY IMPLICATIONS :
Enactment of this bill is necessary to reduce State spending and allow
available cash resources to be used to achieve Financial Plan balance
in 2008-09 and address the projected budget gaps for 2009-10 and
subsequent years.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This bill takes effect immediately.
